<!--
PROMOTED TO THE BODY 2026-08-10 (Luciano) as Figure 5, and the set renumbered around it: the corner
figure became Figure 6 and the usage map Figure 7. This file was figure_6B_four.Rmd; the eight-member
own-tau_int companion (was figure_6BB.Rmd) is figure_5_S1.Rmd, this figure's supplement 1.
WHY IT IS A BODY FIGURE. Every other figure in the set is indexed by the DESIGN (channel count,
noise, sampling interval), which a reader of their own recording does not know. This one is indexed
by a number they measure on their own record with no model and no fit. The Introduction's closing
paragraph makes that offer and, until this promotion, nothing in the paper drew it.
WHAT WAS SETTLED WITH IT, and neither is to be re-opened without a reason:
  FOUR MEMBERS, not three. ILSE, INR, R, IR is the factorial of the two axes, and R is the only
  recursion-without-averaging member; with R dropped, INR is the only one-axis member left and the
  reader attributes the repair to the rest of the ladder in a lump, which 04_results explicitly
  declines to say ("the family cannot be ordered on a single scale").
  ONE SHARED Y, not a scale per panel. The vertical distance between members at the same x IS what
  switching likelihood buys, and per-panel scales destroy exactly that. Second reason, and it is the
  decisive one: IR's internal structure is the estimation floor of the statistic (1.043 +- 0.010,
  see figure_5_variant_2members.Rmd item 4), so a free axis draws the bootstrap at full panel height.
  The free-scale reading belongs to the supplement, which is what it is for.

The x is tau_int of the LEAST-SQUARES residual for every series, because that is what a reader has
before choosing a method; see the note in figure_5_variant_2members.Rmd for why that is the right
independent variable and for why tau_int is not self-referential.

WHY THESE FOUR. They are the 2x2 of the two axes: interval averaging (ILSE, INR have it in their
name; R does not) crossed with recursion (R and IR recurse, ILSE and INR do not). So the panel reads
as a factorial and a reader can see which of the two axes moves the distortion and which does not.

Labels follow figure_4.Rmd:329: nonlinearsqr_g = LSE, nonlinearsqr = ILSE, macro_NR = NR,
macro_INR = INR, macro_R = R, macro_MR = MR, macro_VR = VR, macro_IR = IR.

MEASURED 2026-08-10, and not written up anywhere else yet. The chunk below rebuilds all of it.

  THE DISTORTION HAS A THRESHOLD IN tau_int, BUT ONLY AT A FIXED SAMPLING RATE. Taking size >= 1.15
  as the criterion, the clean and the distorted cells separate without overlap at every sampling
  interval for both gating likelihoods that do not recurse (NR 7 of 7 intervals, INR 7 of 7). The
  two least-squares arms are messier, ILSE 5 of 7 (0.05 and 1 overlap) and LSE 4 of 7 (0.02, 0.5
  and 1). That difference is expected rather than awkward: 04_results.tex:283-289 already records
  that the least-squares ratio also carries the break of its constant-residual-variance premise,
  which is not an information-matrix-equality failure of the same kind.

  POOLED OVER INTERVALS NO THRESHOLD EXISTS, which is the same fact as item (2) of
  figure_5_variant_2members.Rmd.
  At criterion 1.15 the first distorted cell is at tau_int 1.074 while clean cells run to 1.861; at
  1.5 the pair is 1.205 and 1.861; at 2.0 it is 1.205 and 3.002. The reader needs two numbers.

  IR NEVER CROSSES IT IN SIZE, AND DOES CROSS IT IN SHAPE. Its size stays inside 0.982 to 1.077
  over all 294 source cells at both anchors, so zero cells reach 1.15 there. Its shape reaches
  1.419, and 28 of 294 cells sit at or above 1.15, every one of them at N_ch = 10 and the worst at
  noise 0.05, against an estimation floor of 1.043 +- 0.010. That is the Gaussian moment closure on
  the occupancy going at few channels, which 00_abstract.tex already states and which item (4) of
  figure_5_variant_2members.Rmd records as "the only departures are at N_ch = 10". WRITING THIS AS ONE NUMBER IS
  THE MISTAKE THIS FIGURE EXISTS TO PREVENT: a scalar summary cannot express a member that is right
  in the typical direction and wrong across directions, which is the same point item (5) makes
  about least squares at tau_int 1.80.

  R IS THE ONE THAT CAN BE MISREAD OFF THE PANEL, and the caption has to carry the reading. Pooled
  over the twelve noise levels its magnitude median is 1.01, next to IR's 1.00, so the panel LOOKS
  like it says R is calibrated while 04_results says R sits on a floor near 1.4 in k_off. Both are
  right and the dilution is the reason: mag is det(GIDM)^(1/p) over all six directions and most
  cells of the plane are at high noise where every member is calibrated. At noise 0.1 R reads a
  magnitude of 1.143 (1.09-1.24 by channel count) with an anisotropy of 1.19-1.29, so its bar
  reaches 1.48 and the failure is in the BAR, not in the point. This also closes the [OPEN] the
  four-member note carried against decisions.md's 1.46 for R: same pooling, and 1.46 is INR's
  median here, which is worth checking on its own given the NMR/INR history.
  Fraction of cells at or above 1.15 in SIZE, whole ladder:
  LSE 0.495, ILSE 0.524, NR 0.596, INR 0.600, R 0.148, MR 0.386, VR 0.333, IR 0.000.
  Medians and maxima of the size: ILSE 1.37 / 57.2, INR 1.46 / 33.1, NR 1.65 / 2217,
  R 1.01 / 1.26, IR 1.00 / 1.08.

  [CLOSED 2026-08-10] The [OPEN] that stood here, on R reading 1.01 against decisions.md's 1.46,
  is answered above: pooling over the noise axis, verified against the spectrum file. It was NOT
  a different anchor; mag at the sim anchor differs from mag at pool by less than the pooling
  effect. Do not reopen it as an anchor question.

  TWO EDITS THIS FILE STILL OWES, neither of which changes what the figure says.
  (i) THE ILL-CONDITIONED CORNER IS NOT EXCLUDED and it sets the floor of the shared axis. R has
      six cells below magnitude 0.9 (minimum 0.590) and LSE twelve (minimum 0.074), and every one

  (ii) THE X TICK LABELS COLLIDE at four panels across 7 in: the breaks 1, 1.2, 1.5, 2, 3 render as

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE, warning = FALSE, message = FALSE)
suppressMessages({ library(tidyverse) })
```

```{r data}
SRC <- "../figure_4_source_data"
rd  <- function(f) read.csv(file.path(SRC, f), skip = 1, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)

LAB  <- c(nonlinearsqr = "ILSE", macro_INR = "INR", macro_R = "R", macro_IR = "IR")
KEEP <- names(LAB)

tau <- rd("figure_4_source_data_cell_scalars.csv") %>%
  filter(param == "lag", anchor == "pool", algo == "nonlinearsqr") %>%
  transmute(noise, Num_ch, interval_in_tau, tau_int = v)

spec <- rd("figure_4_source_data_spectrum.csv") %>%
  filter(anchor == "pool", algo %in% KEEP) %>%
  select(algo, param, noise, Num_ch, interval_in_tau, m) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = param, values_from = m)

dat <- spec %>%
  inner_join(tau, by = c("noise", "Num_ch", "interval_in_tau")) %>%
  filter(is.finite(mag), is.finite(aniso), mag > 0, aniso > 0) %>%
  mutate(lo = mag / aniso, hi = mag * aniso,
         member = factor(unname(LAB[algo]), levels = unname(LAB)),
         d = factor(sprintf("%g", interval_in_tau),
                    levels = sprintf("%g", sort(unique(interval_in_tau)))))

cat(sprintf("figure_5: %d marks over %d cells; per member: %s\n",
            nrow(dat), n_distinct(dat[c("noise","Num_ch","interval_in_tau")]),
            paste(sprintf("%s=%d", levels(dat$member), as.integer(table(dat$member))),
                  collapse = " ")))
```

```{r render, fig.width = 7.0, fig.height = 3.6}
g <- ggplot(dat, aes(tau_int, mag, colour = d)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 1, linewidth = 0.35, colour = "grey45") +
  geom_linerange(aes(ymin = lo, ymax = hi), linewidth = 0.45, alpha = 0.75) +
  geom_point(size = 0.85) +
  facet_wrap(~ member, nrow = 1) +
  scale_x_log10(breaks = c(1, 1.2, 1.5, 2, 3, 5, 10, 20),
                labels = c("1", "1.2", "1.5", "2", "3", "5", "10", "20")) +
  scale_y_log10(breaks = c(0.3, 0.5, 1, 2, 5, 10, 30, 100, 200),
                labels = c("0.3", "0.5", "1", "2", "5", "10", "30", "100", "200")) +
  scale_colour_viridis_d(name = expression(Delta*t %.% k[off]), option = "D", end = 0.92) +
  labs(x = expression("memory left in the least-squares residual,  "*tau[int]),
       y = "distortion of the reported information\n(point = size, bar = across directions)") +
  theme_bw(base_size = 8, base_family = "Helvetica") +
  theme(panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
        legend.position = "right",
        legend.key.height = unit(9, "pt"),
        strip.background = element_rect(fill = "grey92", colour = NA),
        strip.text = element_text(face = "bold", size = 8))

ggsave("Figure_5.pdf", g, width = 7.0, height = 3.6, device = cairo_pdf)
g
```

```{r numbers}
dat %>% group_by(member) %>%
  summarise(n = n(),
            size_med = median(mag), size_min = min(mag), size_max = max(mag),
            shape_med = median(aniso), .groups = "drop") %>%
  as.data.frame() %>% print(digits = 3)

cat("\nthreshold structure at criterion size >= 1.15, per member and sampling interval:\n")
dat %>% group_by(member, d) %>%
  summarise(tau_max_clean = suppressWarnings(max(tau_int[mag <  1.15])),
            tau_min_dist  = suppressWarnings(min(tau_int[mag >= 1.15])),
            .groups = "drop") %>%
  mutate(separated = ifelse(is.finite(tau_max_clean) & is.finite(tau_min_dist),
                            tau_max_clean < tau_min_dist, NA)) %>%
  as.data.frame() %>% print(digits = 3)
```
